key_insight: A two-stage DeepMD neural-network potential trained for the V-Ti-Cr system captures elastic behavior of V-4Ti-4Cr alloys and predicts how composition and temperature tune stiffness.
engineering_relevance: The results support composition-by-design of vanadium alloys for fusion applications by showing that Cr strengthens while Ti softens the alloy, and that high temperature reduces elastic moduli.
method: MatterSim was used to generate broad configuration sampling for the V-Ti-Cr space.
The potential was fine-tuned to VASP density-functional-theory data.
Large-cell LAMMPS simulations were then used to compute elastic constants at 300 K and 1073 K.
evidence_signal: The reported model accuracy is 9.2 meV/atom for energies and 0.23 eV/angstrom for force components, and it predicts a 1950 K melting temperature for pure V close to experiment.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the coverage of the training set, so extrapolation to compositions, defects, or temperatures outside the sampled domain may be unreliable.
paper_title: Mechanical properties of V-4Ti-4Cr alloy from molecular dynamics with a neural-network potential
